If she had spoken seriously, it would have been quite ridiculous, he thought, even odious, since he had no reason to hate good Charles, not being what one would call consumed by jealousy;—and on that subject, Emma had given him quite a lecture, which he also found in poor taste.
But she was so beautiful!
He had possessed so little of such innocence!
This love without libertinism was something new for him, and it, pulling him out of his easy habits, simultaneously stroked his pride and his sensuality.
Emma's exaltation, which his bourgeois common sense dismissed, seemed to him, deep down, charming, since it was directed at him.
Then, sure of being loved, he did not hold back, and gradually his manner changed.

He no longer had, as before, those sweet words that made her cry, nor those passionate caresses that drove her wild;—so much so that their great love, in which she was immersed, seemed to diminish beneath her, like the water of a river being absorbed into its bed; and she caught sight of the mud.
She did not want to believe it; she increased her tenderness; Rodolphe, less and less, hid his indifference.
She did not know if she regretted having yielded to him, or if she wished, on the contrary, to cherish him even more.
The humiliation of feeling weak turned into a resentment that the pleasures tempered.
It was not attachment, but more like a permanent seduction.
He captivated her.

sentences: After conferring with Sergeant Long, Jasper Hobson decided to grant a day of rest to his companions at this location.
The actual exploration, which was supposed to allow the lieutenant to identify a suitable site for establishing a trading post, was truly about to begin.
The Company had instructed its agent to remain as far north as possible above the seventieth parallel, and along the shores of the Glacial Sea.
However, to fulfill his mandate, the lieutenant could only search to the west for a point that was equally high in latitude and belonged to the American continent.

To the east, in fact, all these fragmented lands are more part of the Arctic territories, except perhaps for Boothia, which is clearly cut by the seventieth parallel, but whose geographical configuration is still very uncertain.
Taking longitude and latitude into account, Jasper Hobson, after marking his position on the map, saw that he was still over a hundred miles below the seventieth degree.

But beyond Cape Kruzenstern, the coast, running northeast, sharply exceeded the seventieth parallel, roughly at the one hundred thirtieth meridian, and precisely at the height of Cape Bathurst, indicated as a meeting point by Captain Craventy.
So it was this point that needed to be reached, and that is where the new fort would be built, if the location offered the necessary resources for a trading post.
"There, Sergeant Long," said the lieutenant, pointing to the map of the polar regions, "there we will be in the conditions imposed on us by the Company.
In this location, the sea, free for a large part of the year, will allow ships from the Bering Strait to reach the fort, supply it, and export its products.
--Not to mention," added Sergeant Long, "that since they will have established themselves beyond the seventieth parallel, our men will be entitled to double pay!
--That goes without saying," replied the lieutenant, "and I believe they will accept it without complaint.
Well, my lieutenant, we only have to leave for Cape Bathurst now," the sergeant simply said.
However, since a day of rest was granted, the departure only took place the next day, June 6.
This second part of the journey was supposed to be and indeed turned out to be completely different from the first.
The arrangements that had governed the sleds' movement until now had not been maintained.
Each team went at its own pace.
We traveled short distances, stopped at every corner of the coast, and most often walked.
Only one recommendation had been made to his companions by Lieutenant Hobson,
the recommendation not to stray more than three miles from the shore and to regroup with the detachment twice a day, at noon and in the evening.
When night fell, we camped.
The weather at that time was consistently nice, and the temperature was quite high, as it averaged fifty-nine degrees Fahrenheit above zero (15° Celsius above zero).

sentences: You have already understood, gentlemen: the device I am describing to you is simply a gas burner using oxygen and hydrogen, whose heat exceeds that of forge fires.
From the lower part of my balloon, which is hermetically sealed, two tubes emerge separated by a small gap.
One originates in the upper layers of hydrogen gas, the other in the lower layers.
These two pipes are equipped at intervals with strong rubber joints, which allow them to adapt to the oscillations of the aerostat.
They both descend to the basket and disappear into a cylindrical iron box, which is called a heat box.
It is closed at both ends by two strong disks made of the same metal.

The pipe coming from the lower region of the balloon enters this cylindrical box through the bottom disk; it penetrates there and then takes the form of a helical coil whose overlapping rings occupy almost the entire height of the box.
Before exiting, the coil goes into a small cone, whose concave base, shaped like a spherical cap, is directed downward.
It is through the top of this cone that the second pipe exits, and it goes, as I told you, into the upper layers of the balloon.
The spherical cap of the small cone is made of platinum.
This is to prevent it from melting under the action of the burner.
For the burner is placed on the bottom of the iron box, in the middle of the helical coil, and the tip of its flame will slightly touch this cap.
You know, gentlemen, what a radiator designed to heat rooms is.
You know how it works.
The air in the room is forced to pass through the pipes, and it is returned at a higher temperature.
Now, what I have just described to you is, in fact, just a radiator.
Indeed, what will happen?
Once the burner is lit, the hydrogen in the coil and the concave cone heats up and quickly rises through the pipe that leads it to the upper regions of the aerostat.

A vacuum forms below, and it draws the gas from the lower regions, which in turn heats up and is continuously replaced; thus, an extremely rapid current of gas is established in the pipes and the coil, exiting the balloon, returning to it, and constantly overheating.

sentences: It is understood that the hunters, for whom hunting quadrupeds was strictly prohibited, passionately turned to the world of birds.
Several hundred of these birds, belonging mainly to edible species, were killed during the first fifteen days, adding a welcome supplement to the usual corn beef and biscuits.
Thus, animals were certainly not lacking in this territory.
The Company could easily stock its stores, and the fort's personnel would not leave their kitchens empty.
However, these two conditions were not enough to ensure the future of the trading post.
One could not settle in a country so far north if it did not provide, and abundantly, the fuel necessary to combat the harshness of Arctic winters.
Fortunately, the coastline was wooded.
The hills, which rose behind the coast, were crowned with green trees, among which the pine predominated.
There were significant clusters of these resinous species, which could be referred to as forests in certain places.
Sometimes, too, in isolated groups, Jasper Hobson noticed willows, poplars, dwarf birches, and numerous arbutus bushes.
At this time of the warm season, all these trees were lush, and they somewhat surprised the eye, accustomed to the stark and bare profiles of polar landscapes.
The ground at the foot of the hills was covered with short grass, which the reindeer eagerly grazed on and which would sustain them during the winter.
As one can see, the lieutenant could only be pleased to have sought out the new site for exploitation in the northwest of the American continent.
It has also been said that while animals were not lacking in this territory, men seemed to be completely absent.
Neither Eskimos were seen, whose tribes prefer to roam the districts closer to Hudson Bay, nor Indians, who do not usually venture this far beyond the Arctic Circle.
And indeed, at this distance, hunters can be caught by continuous bad weather, by a sudden return of winter, and then be cut off from all communication.
One can well imagine that Lieutenant Hobson did not think to complain about the absence of his fellow men.
He could only have found rivals among them.
It was an unoccupied land he was seeking, a desert where fur-bearing animals would likely seek refuge, and in this regard, Jasper Hobson had the most sensible remarks for Mrs.
Paulina Barnett, who was keenly interested in the success of the venture.
The traveler did not forget that she was the guest of the Hudson's Bay Company, and she naturally wished for the lieutenant's plans to succeed.
